intro: Illness and treatment in the language of the doctor's surgery and the leaflet in the box.
p.diagnóstico.consejo: A diagnosis is «dado» or «recibido»: «me dieron el diagnóstico».
p.tratamiento.consejo: It comes from «tratar». You «follow» a treatment: «sigo el tratamiento».
p.síntoma.consejo: It has an accent on the «í»: «SÍN-to-ma». It is masculine: «el síntoma».
p.marearse.glosa: to feel dizzy; to get travel-sick
p.marearse.consejo: The noun is «el mareo»: «me mareo en el coche».
p.tensión.consejo: The tensión is «tomada». «Tener la tensión alta» is having high blood pressure.
p.crónico.consejo: It is said of illnesses: «una enfermedad crónica». It has an accent on the «ó».
p.contagiar.consejo: «Te he contagiado la gripe» and «me he contagiado». The adjective is «contagioso».
p.vacunarse.consejo: It takes «contra»: «vacunarse contra la gripe». The «v» sounds «b».
p.recetar.consejo: The noun is «la receta». It is not «recitar», which is reciting a poem.
p.prospecto.consejo: Careful: in Spanish «prospecto» is not «prospect», but the paper in the medicine box.
p.radiografía.consejo: You «hacer» a radiografía. It is written with «g»: «ra-dyo-gra-FI-a».
p.esguince.consejo: It is, for example, a twisted ankle. The «u» is silent: «es-GIN-the».
p.cicatriz.consejo: In the plural the «z» changes to «c»: «cicatrices».
p.padecer.consejo: It is more formal than «tener». The «yo» form takes «zc»: «padezco».
b1.texto:
**Symptoms.** **Tengo mareos**, **náuseas**, **escalofríos**. **Me mareo** en el coche. **He perdido el apetito.**

**At the surgery.** The doctor **te toma la tensión**, **te manda un análisis de sangre** or **una radiografía**, **te da un diagnóstico** and **te receta** a medicine. Sometimes you are sent to a specialist.

**Illnesses.** An illness can be **leve**, **grave**, **crónica** or **contagiosa**. In formal language you **padecer** or **sufrir** an illness.

**Passing it on.** **Me has contagiado la gripe.** **Me he contagiado.** **Vacunarse contra** la gripe.

**Injuries.** **Hacerse un esguince**, **torcerse el tobillo**, **romperse** a bone. They **escayolan** your arm, put on **una venda**, give you **puntos** and you are left with **una cicatriz**.

**The leaflet.** It gives **la dosis recomendada** and **los efectos secundarios**. A medicine may be **un calmante**, **un antiinflamatorio** or **una pomada**.
b2.f1.texto: I have been dizzy for a week.
b2.f2.texto: I am going to take your blood pressure.
b2.f4.texto: Your blood pressure is very high.
b2.f5.texto: Will I have to follow a treatment?
b2.f6.texto: I am going to prescribe you some pills.
b2.f7.texto: I will read the leaflet very carefully.
b4.titulo: Who acts and what would have happened
b4.texto:
**When others act**, without saying who, Spanish uses the third person plural: **me hicieron una radiografía**, **le dieron cinco puntos**, **me pusieron una venda**.

**Verbs with «se»**: **marearse**, **vacunarse**, **contagiarse**. **Vacunarse contra** la gripe.

**De + compound infinitive** expresses a condition that was not met: **de no haberme caído, no me habría enterado** = if I had not fallen, I would not have found out.
b4.e0.texto: They took an X-ray of my ankle.
b4.e1.texto: Had I not fallen, I would not have found out.
b4.e2.texto: Get vaccinated against the flu every autumn.
b5.f0.texto: The waiting room smells of disinfectant and machine coffee.
b5.f1.texto: A boy swings his legs on the chair while his mother fills in some forms.
b5.f2.texto: I rest my swollen ankle on an empty chair and wait for my turn.
b5.f3.texto: Every step reminds me of this morning's fall, when I was hurrying down the stairs.
b5.f4.texto: A nurse opens the door at the back and calls me by my name.
b5.f5.texto: In a cold, silent room they take an X-ray of my ankle.
b5.f6.texto: The orthopaedic doctor looks at the image calmly and says it is only a sprain.
b5.f7.texto: However, on taking my blood pressure, the nurse frowns.
b5.f8.texto: After several tests they give me the diagnosis, a chronic but mild illness.
b5.f9.texto: Since then I follow the treatment and read the leaflet of every pill carefully.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the prospecto is the paper that comes inside the box.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The radiografía is an image of the bones.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The cicatriz is a mark on the skin.
b6.pregunta: Where do you read how a medicine is taken?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «recetar» is writing down which medicine to take.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Recitar is saying a poem aloud.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Contagiar is passing an illness to someone else.
b7.pregunta: What verb does a doctor use for a medicine?
b8.frase: Le dieron cinco puntos en la frente
b8.traduccion: They gave him five stitches in his forehead
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: marearse is feeling everything spin.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Contagiarse is catching an illness from someone else.
b9.pregunta: What is happening if you feel everything spinning?
b10.frase: Me voy a ____ contra la gripe.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Contagiar passes on an illness; it does not take «contra».
b10.o2.refuerzo: Padecer is suffering an illness, not avoiding it.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «de» + compound infinitive expresses a condition.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That gives a reason; the phrase is about a condition.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That speaks of a moment, not of a condition.
b12.pregunta: «De no haberme caído» is equivalent to…
b12.titulo: A condition that was not met
p.síntomas.consejo: The stress on «síntomas» falls on the first syllable, and the accent stays in the plural.
p.tomarle.consejo: Doctors say «le» meaning you when they are polite. «Tomarle» means to take it from you.
p.seguir.consejo: The gu before e or i sounds like g. So «seguir» is pronounced se-GIR.
p.pastillas.consejo: The double «ll» sounds like a y in most of Spain, so «pastillas» ends in «yas».
p.leeré.consejo: From «leer», to read. Two strong vowels like e-e go in separate syllables.
p.hicieron.consejo: From «hacer», to do. Here it means they took an X-ray. The ie is one stressed syllable.
p.haberme.consejo: From «haber». In «haberme caído» the me stays at the end of the infinitive, like in «verme».
p.vacúnate.consejo: From «vacunarse». The -te at the end is the tú command form of a reflexive verb.
p.contra.consejo: «Contra» means against. Pronounced KON-tra, with the c sounding like k.
p.gripe.consejo: «Gripe» is the common word for the flu. It is always feminine: «la gripe».
p.desinfectante.consejo: From «desinfectar», to disinfect. The c before t sounds like k.
p.balancea.consejo: From «balancear», to swing. The c before e sounds like th in most of Spain.
p.apoyo.consejo: From «apoyar», to lean or rest on something. Here «yo apoyo» means I rest my foot.
p.hinchado.consejo: From «hinchar», to swell up. The ch sounds like the ch in English «church».
p.caída.consejo: From «caer», to fall. The accent on the i breaks the diphthong, so it is ka-I-da.
p.silenciosa.consejo: From «silencio», silence. It describes the room, so it ends in -a: «una sala silenciosa».
p.traumatólogo.consejo: From «trauma», an injury, plus «-logo», a specialist. The stress is on the TO syllable.
p.imagen.consejo: The j-like g before e sounds like an h. In «imagen» say i-MA-hen.
p.tomarme.consejo: From «tomar». The «me» goes at the end, like in «tomarme la tensión».
p.frunce.consejo: From «fruncir», to wrinkle. The c before e sounds like th in Spain.
p.varias.consejo: «Varias» is feminine plural, matching «pruebas». It is said BA-rias.
p.pruebas.consejo: «Prueba» is a test. The ue sounds like one syllable, PRWE, and is written with the u.
p.leve.consejo: The v sounds like b in Spanish, so «leve» is said LE-be.
p.recetó.consejo: From «recetar», to prescribe. The accent on the ó marks the past tense for él or ella.
p.dieron.consejo: From «dar», to give. The ie is one syllable in «dieron», so say DYE-ron.
p.puntos.consejo: «Puntos» also means points or dots. In medicine it means stitches, the little sewn closures.
p.mareo.consejo: From «marear», to make dizzy. The stress is on RE, and the ea-type sound is written as separate vowels.
p.vacunar.consejo: The v sounds like b, so «vacunar» is said ba-ku-NAR. The stress falls on the last syllable.
